papers.title: Same pipelines, different answers: how evaluation design shapes EEG seizure prediction
papers.summary: Holding five published seizure-prediction pipelines fixed and varying only the evaluation design on CHB-MIT, the authors found that subject-held-out partitions yielded near-chance AUCs (0.527–0.553) and that within-patient PSD+LDA dropped from AUC 0.815 with random window allocation to 0.572 with intact preictal blocks, with an index-based split leaking raw samples in all ten eligible cases. They release window manifests, partitions, and predictions for benchmarking.

papers.title: A synchronized dual-scale platform combining flexible micro-ECoG and skull-screw EEG reveals frequency-dependent cortex-to-skull spectral gain in awake mice.
papers.summary: The authors built a synchronized dual-scale platform in awake mice combining a 16-channel flexible micro-ECoG array and five skull-screw EEG electrodes to directly compare cortical and skull-level signals across 115 simultaneous ECoG-EEG pairs. Cortex-to-skull spectral gain increased with frequency following a power law, was non-stationary across protocol blocks, and depended on reference transform, converting cortex-to-skull transfer from a static assumption into a measurable frequency- and state-dependent quantity.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Slow Wave Sleep Detection from Single-Lead EEG in Pediatric Congenital Heart Disease Recovery.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: The authors built the Pediatric Cardiac Post-surgical Sleep (PCPS) expert-annotated polysomnography dataset and PCPS-SleepNet, a multi-band single-lead EEG deep learning framework with a Four-Stage Progressive Encoder and Conformer refinement, pre-trained on public data and fine-tuned on PCPS. Subject-independent validation reached 75.65% accuracy and 89.06% AUROC for staging, and 87.89% AUPRC for slow wave sleep detection.

papers.title: Coordinated Drift of Image Representations in Human EEG
papers.summary: Using the multi-session THINGS-EEG2 dataset, the authors showed that image-evoked EEG response patterns drift across recording sessions in a coordinated, channel-wide manner concentrated along image-identity dimensions, impairing average cross-session decoding while preserving global distance statistics and response-space dimensionality. Simulations indicate Hebbian downstream networks adapt faster to such structured drift than to unstructured drift.

papers.title: Learning discriminative time-frequency representations for EEG segment-level seizure-state classification with channel selection.
papers.summary: The authors proposed a reduced-channel framework combining attention-guided EEG channel selection, TMSST/ConceFT time-frequency analysis, and a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM classifier for segment-level ictal, preictal, and interictal state classification. With a single EEG channel it reached 99.28% accuracy on CHB-MIT and 98.75% on Siena under holdout evaluation, and exceeded 91% accuracy on both databases under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.

papers.title: Diphenhydramine disrupts sleep architecture in 5XFAD Alzheimer's disease model and wild-type mice.
papers.journal: Neurobiology of sleep and circadian rhythms
papers.summary: Chronic oral diphenhydramine (10 mg/kg, one month) was tested in female 5XFAD and wild-type mice with wireless EEG/EMG telemetry; at baseline 5XFAD mice spent more time in NREM1 and had shorter REM and NREM2 bouts, and diphenhydramine fragmented NREM2 in both genotypes, increased NREM1 and REM during the active phase, and disrupted light-dark sleep distribution without rescuing 5XFAD deficits.

papers.title: Style transfer mapping with ensemble learning for cross-subject EEG-based neuropsychiatric disease recognition.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a Prototype-Consistent Style Transfer Mapping framework with confidence-aware transductive semi-supervised adaptation and reliability-aware ensemble learning for cross-subject EEG-based neuropsychiatric disease recognition, reporting stable performance under a leave-one-pair-out protocol on public EEG datasets of major depressive disorder and Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: A representation-level wavelet-EMD fusion framework for spectral analysis and detection of epileptiform patterns in pediatric EEG: computational validation with a roadmap for external benchmarking.
papers.summary: The authors developed a representation-level wavelet-EMD fusion framework with adaptive denoising, energy-criterion EMD, weighted time-frequency fusion, eight spectral-temporal features, and a soft-voting SVM/random forest/neural network ensemble, achieving 94.6% accuracy and AUROC 0.971 on 2,000 synthetic pediatric EEG segments and AUROC 0.901 on CHB-MIT leave-one-subject-out feasibility validation.

papers.title: A generative framework for estimating brain energy landscapes from continuous neuroimaging observations.
papers.summary: The authors introduce a hierarchical generative pairwise maximum entropy model linking latent binary brain states to continuous observations, with node-specific baseline/gain parameters, compound-symmetry noise, and an EEG/MEG leadfield forward model instead of an inverse-first reconstruction. Simulations showed improved recovery of fields, couplings, and latent states, and application to propofol sedation EEG revealed pipeline-dependent condition effects in residual spatial correlation and basin entropy not seen with conventional demean-based pMEM.

papers.title: Clinical utility of electroencephalography-derived aperiodic activity in psychiatric disorders.
papers.summary: This editorial addresses the clinical utility of EEG-derived aperiodic activity in psychiatric disorders; no abstract was supplied, so content details cannot be stated beyond the title's topic.

papers.title: Detection of Spreading Depolarization with Noninvasive Electroencephalography
papers.summary: Developed and validated WAVEFRONT, a noninvasive scalp EEG biomarker of spreading depolarizations based on delta-band spatiotemporal propagation, trained against invasive subdural ECoG in 32 patients with TBI, SAH, or malignant hemispheric stroke (1,119 annotated SDs). WAVEFRONT achieved a cross-validated true positive rate of 97.3±1% at 6.0±0.5% false positive rate, and in an external cardiac-arrest cohort (I-CARE) showed greater SD burden on day 3 in patients with poor versus good neurological outcome (p=0.007).

papers.title: Post-intervention high-beta synchronization tracks stable-manifold alignment during stick-balancing learning
papers.summary: Investigated learning-related changes in control dynamics and beta-band EEG during virtual stick balancing over two days in healthy adults. With practice, balance duration increased, distance to the stable manifold decreased, and post-intervention high-beta synchronization was inversely associated with that distance, suggesting it tracks the quality of transition from active correction to intrinsic control-OFF dynamics.

papers.title: GeoMind: Dancing with Geometric Brain Rhythm on Symmetric Positive Definite Manifolds.
papers.summary: Proposed GeoMind, a geometric state space model neural network that tracks evolving brain states as trajectories on a Riemannian manifold of symmetric positive definite functional connectivity matrices. Reported promising brain-state identification on task fMRI and early diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and autism from resting-state fMRI, and outperformed competing methods on EEG emotion datasets.

papers.title: Robust Epilepsy Diagnosis in Neonates Via Spatio-Temporal Graph Learning and Balanced Test-Time Training.
papers.summary: Presented a cross-subject deep learning framework for neonatal epilepsy diagnosis from EEG that models multichannel signals as spatio-temporal graphs with balanced test-time training for domain adaptation. On 140 neonates (70 healthy, 70 epileptic) it achieved segment-level accuracy of 83% and AUC 0.90, with subject-level accuracy rising from 0.79 to 0.88 with balanced test-time training.

papers.title: BTBD9-driven IMPDH2 ubiquitination governs sleep homeostasis by gating adenosine metabolism in the basal forebrain.
papers.summary: Using human genetic analyses and mouse basal forebrain manipulations, the authors identify a BTBD9-IMPDH2-adenosine pathway in which CRL3-BTBD9 ubiquitinates IMPDH2 at K195 to limit adenosine accumulation, with Btbd9 deletion or AAV interfering peptides increasing NREM sleep and adenosine levels in a manner attenuated by A1R blockade.

papers.title: Magnetoencephalography in Parkinson's disease: diagnostic potential and barriers to clinical translation.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes MEG evidence on spectral activity, functional connectivity, network topology, and brain fingerprinting in Parkinson's disease, reporting recurring spectral slowing and cognitive-network disruption while noting that resting beta power, burst dynamics, and coupling depend on phenotype, treatment state, and analysis choices. It concludes that validated classification of established PD versus controls is promising but does not establish utility in prodromal or uncertain parkinsonism, and calls for standardized, prospectively validated clinical cohorts.

papers.title: Beyond Static Representations: Learning Electroencephalogram Spatiotemporal Dynamics for Enhanced Emotion Recognition.
papers.summary: Proposed DSE-TAM, a framework combining dynamic spatial embedding via graph convolutional networks with a Temporal Attention Mamba module integrating self-attention and state-space models for EEG emotion recognition. Reported accuracies of 79.75%/78.27% (arousal/valence) on DEAP, 80.55%/83.91% on DREAMER, and 73.75% (3-class) on an in-house CEED dataset, surpassing state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Replacing EEG with peripheral physiological signals for driving behavior recognition: a physiology-informed multimodal approach.
papers.summary: Tested whether low-cost peripheral physiological signals (ECG, EMG, GSR) can replace EEG for driving behavior recognition using a physiology-informed multimodal learning framework on a simulator dataset of 35 participants across five driving behaviors. The ECG+EMG+GSR configuration achieved 0.795 accuracy and 0.805 macro-F1 under five-fold cross-validation, outperforming the EEG-only setting and six baseline methods.

papers.title: An EEG-fMRI Jointly Constrained Digital Twin Brain and Its Application in Alzheime's Disease
papers.summary: The authors developed a two-stage digital twin brain framework jointly constrained by fMRI and EEG and validated it in healthy young and Alzheimer's disease cohorts, showing it captures subject-specific multi-scale brain dynamics. AD models reproduced spectral-temporal signatures of cognitive decline linked to simulated excitation-inhibition imbalance, and simulated rTMS responses associated acute EEG normalization with putative E-I rebalancing.

papers.title: Linking Circuit Deficits With Electroencephalography Through Computational Modeling for Psychosis Prediction.
papers.summary: No abstract was supplied, so the specific findings and reported results cannot be summarized; the title indicates a paper linking circuit deficits with electroencephalography through computational modeling for psychosis prediction.

papers.title: Interictal epileptic discharge > 1% associated with cognitive impairment in adult patients with epilepsy: A cross-sectional study based on dose-response relationship and discharge characteristics.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 114 adults with non-symptomatic epilepsy, a sleep interictal epileptiform discharge index >1% was associated with lower MoCA, associative learning, and verbal fluency scores after adjustment, while wakefulness thresholds and lateralization showed no significant graded associations.

papers.title: Levodopa and Subthalamic Nucleus Deep Brain Stimulation Modulate Excitation/Inhibition Balance and the Neural Encoding of Isochronous Sequences in Persons With Parkinson's Disease.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.summary: In persons with Parkinson's disease, EEG analysis showed that levodopa administration and subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation altered β-band event-locked responses, event-related potentials, δ-band neural tracking of isochronous auditory rhythm, and excitation/inhibition balance; changes in E/I were linked to UPDRS-III motor severity under levodopa.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.summary: Systematically reviews deep learning computational approaches for EEG analysis in neurological disease diagnosis, covering CNN, RNN, hybrid, GAN, LLM, autoencoder, and transformer architectures for modeling spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal dynamics across epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and related disorders, alongside preprocessing, denoising, and clinical-translation challenges.

papers.title: EEG-based brain effective and functional connectivity predict PET-defined amyloid positivity in cognitively normal individuals.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: Resting-state dry EEG effective and functional connectivity features trained machine learning models predicting PET-defined amyloid positivity in cognitively normal individuals with accuracy comparable to or exceeding plasma p-tau217 and other predictors, and identified brain regions and connections associated with neurodegeneration.

papers.title: EEG network analysis to identify cortical pathology in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
papers.summary: Graph-theoretical analysis of preoperative EEG in 71 Lennox-Gastaut syndrome patients showed clustering coefficient differentiated surgical outcome groups (AUC 0.915), and a novel Network Dominance Score correctly lateralized the lesion in 100% of patients with favorable resective surgery outcomes.

papers.title: Federated Spiking GANs with Rényi Differential Privacy for privacy-preserving synthetic EEG generation in brain-computer interfaces.
papers.summary: The authors developed a federated spiking GAN framework combining an SNN-based generator, temporally correlated noise, an ANN discriminator, and Rényi differential privacy to generate synthetic EEG data; it preserved temporal features and downstream utility while maintaining privacy relative to RDP-TimeGAN, RDP-CRNN-GAN, RDP-RCGAN, and RDP-Clare-GAN comparators.

papers.title: Neural, vascular, motor and autonomic habituation to high-intensity auditory stimulation: A multimodal characterization of the human defensive responses.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: Using combined EEG, fNIRS and peripheral physiological recordings, the study characterized neural, vascular, motor and autonomic defensive responses to 20 high-intensity white-noise bursts (100 dB) across five blocks. Hemodynamic activation in bilateral auditory and frontal regions declined across blocks with functional connectivity reorganization, and habituation appeared in electrodermal, vascular, motor, ocular and parasympathetic cardiac measures mainly after the first block, while respiratory measures stayed stable and cardiac defense habituation was limited to the late decelerative phase.

papers.title: Impact of hearing loss on visual selective attention: Evidence from N2pc and resting-state networks.
papers.summary: The study compared 34 prelingual deaf, 27 hearing signers and 34 hearing nonsigners on a visual search task with EEG, finding lower hit rates and reduced N2pc amplitudes in deaf individuals along with degraded resting-state alpha network topology (reduced clustering, global efficiency, weaker frontal-occipital connectivity). N2pc amplitude correlated with resting-state network properties and behavioral accuracy, indicating attentional alterations linked to hearing loss rather than sign-language experience.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity of resting EEG in people exposed to armed conflict and controls
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG was compared between 74 Colombian adults exposed to armed conflict and 48 controls, analyzing spectral power and functional connectivity across multiple bands. No EEG contrast survived correction for multiple comparisons, indicating that large or widespread alterations were not detectable; occipital/global alpha power and temporal theta showed only nominal differences.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms of cognitive dysfunction in depression: dual-task event-related potentials and task-phase-dependent EEG functional connectivity.
papers.summary: Compared 30 patients with depression and 30 matched controls using dual-task ERP and task-phase-dependent EEG imaginary-coherence functional connectivity across resting, face-perception (N170), and face mismatch-conflict (N270) phases. Depression showed prolonged N170 latency with reduced amplitude, prolonged N270 latency with increased amplitude, and task-phase-dependent multi-frequency network imbalances; longer N170/N270 latencies correlated with more severe depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Advances in artificial intelligence for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis of neurological diseases: a systematic literature review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA 2020 systematic review screened 842 unique records and included 123 studies on AI for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis of neurological diseases, mapping modalities, architectures, diseases, datasets, and validation practices; heterogeneous populations and incomplete validation extraction precluded ranking diseases, modalities, architectures, or validation strategies.

papers.title: Theta-band EEG changes following sequential rTMS and tACS in fibromyalgia: A randomized controlled pilot study
papers.summary: In an exploratory randomized pilot of 10 fibromyalgia patients, sequential 10-Hz rTMS over left M1 followed by 10 daily bilateral 10-Hz tACS increased resting-state theta EEG power in the active group but not controls, with significant Time × Group and Time × ROI × Group interactions; no effects emerged for delta, alpha, or beta power.

papers.title: Applications of functional ultrasound brain-computer interfaces in neurological diseases: research progress based on neurovascular coupling.
papers.summary: This review examines functional ultrasound (fUS) brain-computer interfaces grounded in neurovascular coupling, covering technical principles, clinical applications in stroke, epilepsy and neurodegenerative disease, and future directions. It reports fUS spatial resolution of about 100 μm and effective temporal resolution of 1-2 s limited by hemodynamic latency, and identifies hemodynamic delay, unclear biosafety of chronic ultrasound exposure, and insufficient decoding reliability in pathological conditions as key bottlenecks for closed-loop acquisition-modulation systems still at proof-of-concept stage.

papers.title: Assessment of the duration of continuous EEG monitoring in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
papers.summary: In a retrospective comparison of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage patients receiving standard 6–7-day versus longer (>7-day) continuous EEG monitoring, longer monitoring was associated with nearly doubled ICU and hospital length of stay but not with vasospasm, delayed cerebral ischemia, or 6-month functional outcome.

papers.title: Impact of burst suppression duration on delirium and its diagnostic value in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 300 mechanically ventilated ICU patients with continuous video-EEG, burst suppression duration was an independent delirium risk factor and predicted delirium with an AUC of 0.871 (cutoff 41.5 s: 80.8% sensitivity, 78.2% specificity); combining burst suppression duration with bispectral index raised the AUC to 0.914.

papers.title: EEG monitoring in the neonate as part of a multimodal brain protection system in paediatric anaesthesia.
papers.journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion
papers.summary: This narrative review examined EEG-based neurological monitoring in neonates during anesthesia as part of multimodal brain protection, drawing on literature from the prior decade. It concludes that brain protection is necessary but that further knowledge and validated technological support are still required.

papers.title: Elaborative processing before retrieval practice enhances semantic organization and long-term memory.
papers.summary: Using EEG, this study compared elaborative processing versus context processing before retrieval practice and found better behavioral memory and 7-day recognition for elaboration. Elaboration elicited a more negative N400 and more positive LPC during encoding, and representational similarity analyses showed stronger semantic-category organization and greater representational reorganization.

papers.title: Making sense of touch: Spatial tactile cues promote efficient visuo-somatosensory integration and restore motor accuracy under sensory conflict.
papers.summary: Healthy adults performed a mirror-tracing task under visuo-somatosensory conflict while receiving tactile feedback with or without explicit spatial landmarks. Spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness and were associated with increased somatosensory activity and more restricted sensorimotor connectivity, whereas non-spatial touch was linked to widespread cortical reductions and diffuse connectivity.

papers.title: A mechanistic classification of GNAO1 mutations links Gβ γ sequestration to hyperkinetic disease and treatment response
papers.summary: Integrated human genetic analysis with cellular assays to classify GNAO1 variants into those that sequester Gβγ versus those reducing Go expression, showing that impaired Gβγ release is associated with the hyperkinetic NEDIM phenotype. In GNAO1R209H/+ mice, caffeine and gallein both reduced hyperlocomotion, and patch-clamp recordings revealed sex- and cell-type-specific hyperexcitability in dorsolateral striatal spiny projection neurons.

papers.title: SCN2B Drives Depression-like Phenotypes in Mice by Suppressing BDNF Signaling via Its Intracellular Domain NICD.
papers.summary: Using SCN2B-overexpressing mice and NICD-reduced Navβ2V173A,V175K mice, this study shows that SCN2B overexpression drives depression-like phenotypes via NICD-dependent suppression of BDNF/TrkB/PI3K/AKT signaling and region-specific excitatory/inhibitory imbalance in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. NICD-reduced mice were resistant to chronic unpredictable mild stress, implicating Navβ2 proteolysis as a therapeutic target.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
